candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record documents pulsatile arterial bleeding from the right ureteral orifice on stent removal, CT angiogram showing active hemorrhage at the right renal pelvis, and recurrent massive hematuria requiring renal artery embolisation — all pointing to a ureteroarterial fistula. Hemorrhagic cystitis is a bladder mucosal condition and does not account for pulsatile arterial bleeding at the ureteral orifice, the angiographic findings, or the response pattern described. While radiation exposure is present in the history and could be a contributing etiologic factor to a ureteroarterial fistula, the candidate asserts a different anatomical structure (bladder) and a different pathological entity (mucosal hemorrhage vs. arterial fistula).
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Radiation-induced hemorrhagic cystitis is a bladder-origin diagnosis; the reference is a ureteroarterial fistula, an arterial communication with the ureter

case_quality_flags: Classic ureteroarterial fistula presentation: long-term ureteral stenting, pelvic radiation, pulsatile arterial bleeding at ureteral orifice, angiographic confirmation
